neighbours.label: a topological object in gauge theory: instanton, monopole, skyrmion, vortex, winding number, global anomaly
fire: The BPST instanton minimizes the action in Euclidean space.
A Dirac monopole would explain the quantization of charge.
Witten found a global anomaly in the SU(2) theory with one doublet.
The Skyrme soliton is stabilized by its nonzero winding number.
Abrikosov vortex lines carry quantized magnetic flux in a superconductor.
Gauge fields are classified by their second Chern number on the sphere.
Each field configuration has an integer topological charge.
A 't Hooft monopole appears when the SU(2) symmetry is broken.
quiet: The W boson minimizes nothing, and it decays in a fraction of a second.
A Dirac spinor would explain the spin of the electron.
Witten gave a popular lecture on the SU(2) theory at Princeton.
The neutron star is stabilized by its nuclear pressure.
Copper transmission lines carry electric current in a cable.
Gauge fields are written in terms of a potential on the blackboard.
Each electron has a negative electric charge.
A Higgs boson appears when the two beams collide.

notes: A second round after the sweep label ' anomaly in physics' failed: only 'global anomaly' fired there, and ' instanton' after SU(2) fired on a near miss. Probes here: instanton 0.72, topological 1.04, skyrmion 0.90, against gluon 0.04, doublet 0.24.
